title: COPD, respiratory failure and home oxygen
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's chronic lung disease and any respiratory failure or oxygen dependence.
note:
Chief Complaint
Shortness of breath and increased cough.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a follow-up regarding his chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He reports a recent exacerbation of his symptoms over the last week, characterized by increased dyspnea and a productive cough. He notes that his breathing has felt significantly more difficult than his baseline. He continues to use home oxygen daily to manage his symptoms.

Medication List
1. Prednisone 40mg daily (started today)
2. Tiotropium
3. Salbutamol inhaler as needed

Exam
The patient appears in mild respiratory distress. Lung sounds reveal diminished breath sounds and expiratory wheezes bilaterally. Oxygen saturation is 91% on his current supplemental oxygen flow. No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation.
2. Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia.

Plan
The patient will begin a 5-day steroid burst of Prednisone 40mg daily to address the current exacerbation. He was instructed to monitor his oxygen levels and contact the clinic if symptoms worsen. He will continue his current home oxygen regimen.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 05/12/2026
explanations: COPD with an acute exacerbation: J44.1 (same HCC 280 as stable COPD, but a different code).
Chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia: J96.11 (HCC 213), plus Z99.81 for the home oxygen.

distractors.why: An acute exacerbation is documented: J44.1.
The provider diagnoses chronic respiratory failure: J96.11 (HCC 213).
Only chronic respiratory failure is documented.

hccs.label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease/Interstitial Lung Disorders/and Other Chronic Lung Disorders
